Commentary.Commentary: We are back, and probably for the final time in this Test. With just 8 runs to win, the Kiwis will be in a hurry to wrap things up. Will Young and Devon Conway are out in the middle for the Kiwis, whereas Newman Nyamhuri will bowl the first over for Zimbabwe in the second innings with three slips in place, along with one gully. Here we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Meanwhile, in The Oval, England's reply has been swift and dominant. Openers Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett came out with aggressive intent, putting on a rapid 92-run partnership. Duckett was the more explosive of the two, scoring a quickfire 43 before being caught behind off Akash Deep's bowling. However, the wicket did little to slow England's momentum, as Crawley has continued to score freely, reaching an unbeaten 52. Supported by captain Ollie Pope, England currently stands at 109 for 1 after just 16 overs, showcasing a commanding response to India's total.

The Kiwis' bowling attack was clinical and ruthless! Matt Henry and Will O'Rourke took 3 wickets each, with their skipper Mitchell Santner taking 4, showcasing their skill and precision. Despite dealing with injuries, including Nathan Smith's abdominal tear and Will O'Rourke's back issue, the Kiwis didn't let that affect their performance. They bowled Zimbabwe out for a modest score, setting up an easy 8-run chase for themselves.

Zimbabwe's top order struggled, getting bundled out cheaply in the second innings. Despite some resistance from Sean Williams, Craig Ervine, and a gritty 9th-wicket partnership between Tafadzwa Tsiga and Blessing Muzarabani, the hosts couldn't put up a solid score on the board. The top order's lack of grit and determination cost them dearly, as Tafadzwa Tsiga, Sean Williams, and Ervine showed flashes of fight that might have changed the game if shown by the top order.
The Kiwis have a cakewalk ahead of them! Zimbabwe's second innings has been wrapped up for 165, setting a target of just 8 runs for New Zealand to chase.

OUT! CAUGHT! DONE! Zimbabwe have been bowled out for 165 and New Zealand need just eight runs to win the game. Santner tosses it up and keeps it around off, Tafadzwa Tsiga gets down on his knee and looks to go for a big lofted shot downtown, but the ball is slow and too close to his body. Generates a top edge that goes in the air towards cover point, where Devon Conway moves to his left and goes to catch it low around his knee height, but fails to grab it in the first attempt. The ball lobs up, and Conway manages to snatch it and grab it on the second attempt. Santner smiles there, having his hands on his head, as he would have believed that it would also go down, but Devon manages to take it, and Zimbabwe have managed a lead of just 7 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the post-Lunch session. Zimbabwe are in a situation of bother, and it will take some knock from Raza, supported by Tafadzwa Tsiga and the tail to bail them out of here. Raza and Tsiga are ready to have a go at the Kiwi bowlers, and it will be Matt Henry to bowl the first over of this session with three slips and one gully in place. Also, Will O'Rourke hasn't taken the field as a part of precaution, and the reason is that he has felt a bit of back stiffness, and Jacob Duffy, the substitute fielder, is on the field for him, as per the on-air commentators. This means New Zealand are two bowlers short now.

Meanwhile, in The Oval for the fifth and final Test for the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy, India's first innings began with a shaky start on Day 1, losing key wickets early, with Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul falling cheaply. The Indian middle-order, led by Sai Sudharsan and Shubman Gill, tried to steady the ship, but England's bowlers, particularly Josh Tongue, continued to make inroads with his occasionally peach deliveries. Despite the regular fall of wickets, a good partnership between Karun Nair and Washington Sundar helped India reach 204 for 6 by the end of Day 1. However, the next morning on Day 2, today, the remaining four wickets fell rapidly for just 20 more runs, with Gus Atkinson claiming five wickets. India have been bowled out for 224, leaving England to take control of the Test match.

Heading into the second session, the match is clearly tilting heavily in New Zealand’s favour. Zimbabwe still trail by 44 runs with only four wickets remaining, and unless Raza plays a gritty knock and finds support from Tsiga, this Test might not last till Day 4. The pitch is showing uneven bounce, which will further challenge the batters as the day progresses. New Zealand will be keen to wrap things up quickly and seal a strong win. All eyes will now be on the post-Lunch session, which will start at 10.40 am GMT.

For New Zealand, this session was all about control and execution. Will O'Rourke continued bowling tight lines and generating bounce, taking two wickets in the session. Matt Henry, who had started a bit wide outside off early on, adjusted brilliantly to pick up a key wicket before Lunch. The skipper, Mitchell Santner, has bowled with control as well, extracting some turn and bounce to remove the dangerous Williams. The variation in bounce, movement off the surface, and consistent pressure from all bowlers have kept Zimbabwe on the back foot throughout the session. Tom Blundell also deserves credit for sharp work behind the stumps, taking three catches so far in this first session.

One of the major concerns for Zimbabwe has been the lack of application from their batters. Apart from brief partnerships and individual moments of resistance, most of the top and middle order have failed to dig in and show the kind of temperament required in Test cricket. There has been a recurring pattern, either chasing deliveries they could have left or falling into soft dismissals under pressure. The skipper, Craig Ervine, too, was trying to anchor the innings, showing patience and experience under pressure. But right after Williams’ dismissal, he too fell, this time to Matt Henry, who bowled a probing spell in his second burst before Lunch. With both senior players gone in quick succession, Zimbabwe’s hopes of resisting have taken a serious hit.

Zimbabwe began the day with overnight batters Nick Welch and Vincent Masekesa looking to survive and build. They were cautious in their approach, trying not to chase wide deliveries and playing close to the body. However, it didn’t take long for Will O'Rourke to break through, as he got Welch caught behind with a delivery that just held its line, and later cramped Masekesa for room, forcing a glove to short leg. The real fight came from Williams and Ervine, who added a crucial 57-run stand. Williams, in particular, looked in fine touch, finding the gaps and rotating strike well. Unfortunately, just when he looked set for a well-deserved half-century, he feathered one down the leg side to the keeper, falling for 49.

New Zealand have dominated the morning session on Day 3, tightening their grip firmly on the 1st Test match in Bulawayo. Coming into the day with Zimbabwe trailing by 127 runs, the Kiwis struck early and often, picking up four wickets in this session alone. The Zimbabwean top-middle order has tried to show some resistance, especially through the experienced duo of Sean Williams and Craig Ervine, but New Zealand’s bowlers have been relentless. Two quick wickets just before the Lunch break, including that of the well-set Williams for 49 and Ervine soon after, have pushed Zimbabwe further into trouble. At Lunch, Zimbabwe find themselves six down, still trailing by 44 runs, and the match could well finish today if this collapse continues.

FOUR! A boundary to end the first session on Day 3. Short, down leg. Sikandar Raza moves inside the line of it, gets down on a knee and sweeps this through the vacant backward square leg region for a boundary. Zimbabwe ends this session trailing by 44 runs now. That will be LUNCH ON DAY 3!

Commentary.Commentary: All is set for the action to kick off for Day 3 in Bulawayo. The umpires walk out, and so have the players of New Zealand to take their respective positions. But before that, they get in a huddle for a pep talk and then spread out. Also, walk out two the unbeaten overnight batters of Zimbabwe, where Nick Welch will resume the batting along with nightwatchman Vincent Masekesa. Will O'Rourke will start the proceedings with three slips in place. Here we go...

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford and Scott Styris are pitchside. According to Scott Styris, the Airport End produces a tennis-ball bounce that can trouble batters, especially against taller bowlers like Will O'Rourke, while the City End has a lower bounce that encourages front-foot play. The morning session is likely to be challenging due to residual moisture, making it vital for Zimbabwe to navigate this period with minimal losses. The key for both teams will be to adapt to the pitch conditions and capitalize on opportunities.

Also, Dion Ebrahim, the batting coach of Zimbabwe, is up for a quick chat before the start of today's play. He reflects on the team's ongoing efforts to build consistency across all formats. Says that it isn't that simple to answer in one sentence, but the coaching group had been working hard to implement a clear approach, with a focus on structure and discipline, along with consistency. While acknowledging that batting success could be subjective and influenced by many variables, he emphasises the team's intent to bat deeper into innings and convert starts into significant scores. Highlights one of the key positives over the past year, as Zimbabwe have an increased number of centuries. However, he stresses that the focus remained on achieving that consistency through refining technical abilities. According to him, both senior and younger players need to step up, as it ultimately came down to the discipline required to apply themselves for long periods at the crease. Admits that the side had been a bit scrappy in patches but remains hopeful for a more measured and disciplined second-innings display. Reiterates the importance of executing the game plan, particularly in Test cricket, where clarity of role and patience often make the biggest difference.

Devon Conway of New Zealand is up for a chat. Conway feels that the pitch was quite challenging, especially with the new ball, due to the bounce on the surface and the bowlers' ability to extract movement. Highlights the importance of the partnership with Will Young in putting pressure on the bowlers and the team's strategy of batting for long periods and riding out tough phases. Conway emphasises the need to stay positive, communicate effectively, and capitalise on loose deliveries to put pressure back on the bowlers. Conway notes that the team made some adjustments in the second innings, such as standing deep in the crease to better deal with the bounce and reading the length more effectively. He believes the morning session will be crucial for New Zealand to pick up wickets and acknowledges that there's still plenty in it for the bowlers. Regarding the bowling attack, Conway expresses hope that Nathan Smith would be fit enough to bowl later in the innings, but has full confidence in Matt Henry and Will O'Rourke to make early inroads.

As we build toward the action on Day 3, all eyes will be on Zimbabwe’s middle order. Can they channel the grit they showed with the ball into their batting? Or will New Zealand’s attack, even one short, sniff blood early and race toward victory? One thing’s for certain - the thrill of battling. Also, the pitch at Queens Sports Club has remained relatively slow but is beginning to show signs of wear. With that, stay tuned for more, as the action isn’t far away!

For Zimbabwe, there are some positives, but much still to do. Their bowlers fought back admirably after the Conway–Young stand. But batting remains a concern. They struggled to rotate strike in the first innings, and now in the second, both openers are already gone. Nick Welch and nightwatchman Vincent Masekesa have a big job today to blunt the attack. With experienced names like Williams, Ervine, and Raza still to come, there's hope, but only if they bat time and apply themselves better than they did on Day 1. Survival first, then rebuild. They can’t afford another collapse here.

New Zealand will feel they’re in control, and the margin is quite strong, allowing them to even win the first match by an inning. Daryl’s knock was the glue holding things together, and Nathan Smith’s brave 22 before retiring hurt was a huge moment. The abdominal tear that now rules Smith out of bowling leaves the Kiwis a bowler short, meaning their spinners, Mitchell Santner and Michael Bracewell, will have more work to do. Also, the pace duo of Matt Henry and Will O'Rourke will need to operate efficiently. With a lead of 127 already and eight wickets to take, they will look to strike early and push for a result in the first two sessions, considering how Zimbabwe batted in their first inning.

The story so far has unfolded in three compelling acts. Zimbabwe were bundled out for 149 in their first innings despite some resistance from Craig Ervine and Tafadzwa Tsiga. New Zealand, in reply, surged to 92/0 by Stumps on Day 1 with Will Young and Devon Conway setting the tone. Day 2, however, turned chaotic for the Kiwis as Blessing Muzarabani struck with the first ball, triggering a collapse of sorts. Conway’s defiant 88 and Daryl Mitchell’s resolute 80 ensured New Zealand posted 307, securing a 158-run lead. Zimbabwe struck back in the final session with the ball, but once again stumbled with the bat, losing both openers quickly to Matt Henry and Will O'Rourke. They now have a mountain to climb if they want to stay in this contest.

Hello and welcome to Day 3 of the first Test between Zimbabwe and New Zealand from Bulawayo, commonly known in cricketing folklore as ‘Moving Day’. The match has already witnessed dramatic shifts in momentum, and as the middle day dawns, both sides have much to play for. After a grind on Day 1 and a fascinating ebb and flow on Day 2, New Zealand find themselves ahead on the scorecard. Zimbabwe, meanwhile, having shown grit with the ball, now face a stern test with the bat after ending Day 2 at 31/2 in their second innings, still trailing by 127 runs. More than ten wickets fell on the second day, and with variable bounce creeping in, Day 3 could be pivotal, perhaps even decisive.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from an entertaining Day 2 of this 1st Test, where New Zealand are still in the driving seat, but Zimbabwe improved a lot from the opening day. The game is nicely poised as we shift towards the 'Moving Day.' If the Kiwis can skittle out the hosts quickly, and there are signs of that, we could possibly see a result on Day 3. It is looking increasingly likely as of now, unless Zimbabwe bats their skins out. The action resumes on 1st August, Friday, at 8 am GMT, but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

In the final session, even with the second new ball in hand, Zimbabwe couldn’t break through New Zealand’s lower order quickly, allowing the visitors to stretch their lead with Daryl Mitchell and Nathan Smith leading the charge. Mitchell crafted a fine 80, while Smith was forced to retire hurt with an abdominal tear, ruling him out of bowling in this innings - a setback for the Kiwis. However, they responded strongly with the ball as Matt Henry and Will O'Rourke struck early to remove both openers. But Nick Welch, along with nightwatchman Vincent Masekesa, ensured no further damage was done before Stumps.

If Zimbabwe showed fight in the first session, they certainly made New Zealand work hard for every run in the next. The bowlers stuck to disciplined lines and lengths, and Tanaka Chivanga’s dismissal of Devon Conway set things in motion. Skipper Sean Williams rotated his attack smartly, and the hosts were rewarded with four key wickets, making them the dominant side in that session.

Zimbabwe began Day 2 in style as Blessing Muzarabani struck with the very first ball, removing Will Young. However, they had to work hard after that, as the Kiwi batters dug in and kept the scoreboard ticking. Their persistence eventually paid off when Tanaka Chivanga and Sikandar Raza claimed a couple of quick wickets. Through it all, Devon Conway held firm for the visitors and, with support from his partners, guided New Zealand into the lead by Lunch.

An action-packed Day 2 comes to a close! Zimbabwe displayed plenty of grit and determination, particularly with the ball, but their batting struggles remain. They succeeded in limiting New Zealand’s lead to 158 runs, yet lost both openers in the challenging period before Stumps and now trail by 127 runs.

A confident appeal from the Kiwis but nothing barring a smile from the umpire as he turns it down. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 2!
